messages.subject: Hey, I used Stan too
parts:
I saw some dissertations on the "citation" page, so I'm piling on.  From the Uni page:

Recommended Citation

Sakrejda, Krzysztof M., "Estimation Problems in Complex Field Studies with Deep Interactions: Time-to-Event and Local Regression Models for Environmental Effects on Vital Rates" (2015). Doctoral Dissertations May 2014 - current. Paper 510.
http://scholarworks.umass.edu/dissertations_2/510

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hey, I used Stan too
parts:
On this note, I’ve noticed a lot of papers that cite Stan but haven’t been put on that page. Is this process of suggesting it through stan-users the right way to get them in? Is a public wiki too dangerous to do instead? I imagine that page will be enormous and hard to maintain.

Dustin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hey, I used Stan too
parts:
No, this won't be best for coverage. Most people won't think
to tell us about their publications using Stan.

And among those who do, GitHub pul requests are a high hurdle.

For now, I don't mind adding publications from users who send
them to us, but this may quickly get too big to manage and need
to be something more like a public Wiki.

- Bob
